# the contributor audit: strict R4 affine equality and uniform facet localization

Sources: `candidate 45b8df25a0cd5956` and Section 7 of `candidate 810352ec6ea27062`. Independent root audit: PASS, with the fixed-marginal and own-center premises retained.

For the R4 discriminator, the previously audited exact martingale has row mass 22, column mass 9, and preserves base coordinates. Summing its nonnegative convex Jensen gaps gives exactly Delta(b). If Delta vanishes, each positive row gap vanishes and b is affine on its target hull. The fourteen-row propagation uses a full affine basis of each row's hull already covered by earlier rows. Consequently the affine functions agree on the relevant hulls and extend one initial affine function to all 31 bases. The standalone verifier confirms every positive row balance, basis containment, affine rank, propagation step and full-base coverage in 181 exact checks. The three outer vertices and their strict interior barycenter zero then force affinity throughout D4 by Jensen equality. Conversely affine functions make Delta zero.

Any physical martingale retaining those exact moved high/low marginals on a common facet graph must preserve the affine physical coordinate lambda_i in total. It therefore makes Delta(b_i)=0, regardless of its chosen transport edges. This conclusion requires the specified marginals. It does not assert that a deformed low-efficiency profile retains those marginals or supplies them automatically.

For uniform facet localization, strict affine support of each b_i at the source base gives an affine physical functional constant on that whole source facet and uniformly lower on every other same-normal facet. A small positive hinge is therefore constant on the source facet and zero on all other bases' corresponding facets. Normal selectors separate the finitely many oriented facet normals. Scaling each hinge by the source-centered radial flux on its facet and summing reproduces exactly that flux on the source boundary and zero elsewhere. The scaling is nonnegative because the selected point is in the own-fiber interior. The divergence theorem yields denominator d times own volume and each through-source cap contribution d times own cap volume, with pure-base through-source caps capturing the whole own fiber. Thus the weighted efficiency is exactly the weighted own-cap fraction and at least ordinary depth of the selected point. Gamma follows at an actual ordinary Gamma center, in particular the own centroid. No arbitrary noncentroid guarantee is inferred.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
